title: When the Cross-Silo Federation Goes Offline: Continual Learning for Site Onboarding with Limited Unlabeled Data
alt: Architecture of offline site onboarding with class-specific autoencoders, novelty detection, and model expansion
summary: Onboards a new site after a federation goes offline, using limited unlabeled data to discover unfamiliar classes and adapt the model while retaining existing knowledge.
method: Combines federated class-specific denoising autoencoders, reconstruction-based novelty detection, clustering, and selective classifier expansion. Compares local rehearsal, shared prototypes, and a combination of both.
evaluation: Evaluated on ultrasonic metal welding across five seeds. The dual-rehearsal variant achieves 88.9% mean accuracy on both old and new classes in the autonomous onboarding experiment. Results concern a controlled manufacturing study; prototype sharing and local rehearsal have different data-disclosure requirements.

title: LLM-ADAM: A Generalizable LLM Agent Framework for Pre-Print Anomaly Detection in Additive Manufacturing
alt: LLM-ADAM workflow with Extractor, Reference, and Judge agents and deterministic Python analysis
summary: Turns machine instructions into evidence for defect diagnosis through specialized LLM agents and deterministic analysis.
method: An Extractor structures G-code parameters, a Reference agent grounds operating ranges in documentation, Python computes deviations, and a Judge diagnoses defects using the resulting evidence.
evaluation: The best configuration achieves 87.5% accuracy versus 59.5% for a single-LLM baseline on 200 G-code programs spanning two printers, two materials, and five classes. The reported results cover controlled program-level diagnosis.

feature.label: LLM-ADAM
feature.title: LLM agents & tool use
feature.description: An agent framework combining structured extraction, grounded references, and deterministic tools for evidence-based diagnosis.

title: Adaptive unknown fault detection and few-shot continual learning for condition monitoring in ultrasonic metal welding
alt: Open-set fault detection and few-shot continual learning pipeline for ultrasonic metal welding
summary: Detects faults outside a model’s known classes, groups unfamiliar examples, and learns new fault classes from a small labeled sample.
method: Builds class-specific acceptance regions in a learned embedding, uses clustering to support labeling, and updates selected classifier layers while freezing most parameters.
evaluation: Reports 96% unknown-fault detection accuracy and up to 98% overall classification accuracy after a five-sample update in the single-new-class experiment. Only 9.2% of model parameters are trained during adaptation. The study assumes a consistent underlying process and sensor configuration.

feature.label: Adaptive fault learning
feature.title: Continual learning & anomaly detection
feature.description: Detecting unfamiliar classes and adapting a model from a few labeled examples while retaining existing knowledge.

title: QoS-QoE Translation with Large Language Model
alt: Literature-grounded data pipeline linking quality of service and quality of experience
summary: Builds a source-grounded dataset of multimedia quality relationships and evaluates LLMs that translate between network performance and perceived user experience.
method: Combines literature curation, structured relationship extraction, iterative evaluation, and supervised fine-tuning for bidirectional QoS–QoE prediction.
evaluation: Includes 1,026 relationship records and 8,107 derived chat instances. Evaluates continuous values and discrete labels, retaining source evidence and context for each relationship.

title: FDM-bench: a domain-specific benchmark for evaluating large language models in additive manufacturing
alt: Printed objects showing normal, under-extruded, over-extruded, and spaghetti defect classes
summary: Benchmarks LLM manufacturing knowledge and G-code interpretation against expert-reviewed questions and real printing outcomes.
method: Pairs 16 G-code programs and four printing classes with 30 free-response and 75 multiple-choice questions at three expertise levels. Fourteen domain experts review the evaluation material.
evaluation: Compares GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Llama models to expose gaps between general language competence and manufacturing-specific reasoning. The benchmark and evaluation code are public.

feature.label: FDM-Bench
feature.title: LLM evaluation & benchmarking
feature.description: An expert-reviewed benchmark testing language-model knowledge, reasoning, and program analysis against measurable outcomes.

title: MachineStethoscope: A Smart and Cost-effective Machine Health Monitoring System
alt: MachineStethoscope edge data acquisition and compression-based anomaly detection architecture
summary: Uses inexpensive sensing and compression-based analysis to monitor equipment anomalies at the edge while reducing data storage and transmission.
method: Converts high-rate sensor signals to spectrogram sequences and uses video compression behavior to identify changes in temporal regularity.
evaluation: Evaluated on real laboratory vacuum pumps and controlled failure sequences. The study detects eight real pump anomaly events and reduces the size of transmitted data by over 90% in the evaluated setup.

title: Multi-Modal Zero-Shot Prediction of Color Trajectories in Food Drying
alt: Multimodal trajectory prediction architecture combining process parameters and initial food images
summary: Fuses initial images with process settings to predict full color-change trajectories under unseen drying conditions, without condition-specific fine-tuning.
method: Uses compact trajectory basis functions, image features, process parameters, and similarity-informed training-set selection.
evaluation: Validated on cookie and apple drying. For apples, the best multimodal configuration reaches RMSE 1.2865 versus 10.1517 for the reported baseline. Here, zero-shot refers to unseen combinations of drying conditions.

title: Federated domain generalization for condition monitoring in ultrasonic metal welding
alt: Federated learning system with a shared feature extractor and task-specific condition-monitoring heads
summary: Learns shared representations and personalized tasks across manufacturing sites, improving condition monitoring on unseen domains without pooling raw sensor data.
method: Combines a shared base model, task-specific upper layers, group-wise aggregation, and regularization. Includes an edge–cloud implementation with Raspberry Pi clients and RabbitMQ.
evaluation: Reports gains of 5.35–8.08 percentage points over the compared federated baselines on unseen-domain tasks. FTL-TP is the earlier preprint of this work.

feature.label: FDG-CM
feature.title: Federated learning & generalization
feature.description: Distributed learning with shared representations and personalized models, evaluated on data from previously unseen domains.

title: WeldMon: A Cost-effective Ultrasonic Welding Machine Condition Monitoring System
status: Conference paper · Best Student Paper Award
alt: WeldMon architecture and laboratory deployment on an ultrasonic welding machine
summary: Combines low-cost sensing, learned and engineered features, and data augmentation for autonomous welding-condition monitoring on a Raspberry Pi.
method: Uses an audio ADC for high-rate acquisition, converts multimodal signals to image-like inputs, and combines CNN features with signal features for classification.
evaluation: The evaluated system costs as little as $120. The hybrid pipeline averages approximately 385 ms per processing cycle on a Raspberry Pi 4; performance is evaluated across tool and surface-condition tasks.

title: Classification of Activities of Daily Living Based on Grasp Dynamics Obtained from a Leap Motion Controller
alt: Experimental setup for measuring hand grasp dynamics with a Leap Motion Controller
summary: Recognizes daily-living activities using three-dimensional hand motion and grasp dynamics captured by a Leap Motion Controller.
method: Transforms hand coordinates to remove gross movement, normalizes geometric features, and compares support vector machines with convolutional classifiers.
evaluation: Studies eight activities in eight healthy participants with five-fold cross-validation. The best reported activity-detection CNN reaches 99.88% accuracy and 97.3% macro recall; patient evaluation remains future work.

title: A new scheme for the development of IMU-based activity recognition systems for telerehabilitation
alt: Wearable inertial sensors positioned on a participant for activity-recognition experiments
summary: Optimizes wearable sensor placement and signal features, then adapts activity-recognition models with a small amount of participant-specific data.
method: Uses genetic search over sensors and signals, time/frequency/wavelet features, dimensionality reduction, and several classifiers. Healthy-participant data support the initial design.
evaluation: Evaluates 34 activities using nine healthy participants and two participants with Parkinson’s disease. The small patient cohort supports a preliminary adaptation study.

title: Optimal Sensor Configuration for Activity Recognition during Whole-body Exercises
alt: Whole-body exercise examples used to evaluate inertial sensor configurations
summary: Searches sensor configurations and signal features for efficient recognition of whole-body rehabilitation exercises, with adaptation for new users.
method: Uses genetic optimization over wearable IMU configurations and engineered signal features with a nearest-mean classifier.
evaluation: Evaluates 34 activities in nine healthy participants. The work establishes the sensor-selection and adaptation approach developed further in the 2022 journal article.
